title: Prominent NYC rabbi’s daughter accuses Mamdani of fueling antisemitism: ‘I’m sure many have buyer’s remorse’
text:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

The daughter of a prominent rabbi whose Manhattan synagogue was swarmed by vile anti-Israel and antisemitic protesters last fall accused Mayor Zohran Mamdani of fueling “Jewish hatred” in New York City.

Karen Schneier Dresbach — who is executive vice president of the multi-faith Appeal of Conscience Foundation as well as the daughter of Rabbi Arthur Schneier of Park East Synagogue — said she believes some Jews who voted for Mamdani are having “buyer’s remorse.”

“When you have a mayor of the city of New York, who continues to spew rhetoric … this just fuels Jewish hatred in our city,” Schneier Dresbach said Sunday on 770 WABC’s the “Cats Roundtable” program.

Mamdani is a staunch critic of Israel.

He supports the Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions movement against the country, refuses to recognize it as a Jewish state and has urged New Yorkers to protest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s visit to Manhattan next month during the United Nations General Assembly, accusing him of being a war criminal.

She claimed Jews who voted for Mamdani have learned a harsh lesson.

“To Jews who voted socialist and for Mamdani,… sometimes you learn the hard way. What did they say in The Wizard of Oz? ‘Don’t pay attention to the man behind the curtain.’ … I’m sure many [Jews] have buyer’s remorse – certainly with regard to their votes for Mayor Mamdani,”  Schneier Dresbach said.

Schneier Dresbach said antisemitism has exploded after Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023 attack on Israel and the subsequent war in Gaza.

In an example close to home, her father Arthur Schneier’s historic Upper East Side synagogue was targeted by menacing anti-Israel protesters last year.

The Holocaust-surviving 96-year-old, who founded the organization where Schneier Dresbach is executive vice president, told The Post last November that the protest left him shaken.

“I don’t know how you expect a man to feel who saw his synagogue burn to the ground as a child and now has his synagogue attacked twice in the United States — and now to witness, almost on a daily basis, the egregious attacks, these heinous attacks on houses of worship, synagogues, [on Jews] … It’s insanity!” Schneier Dresbach said.

“The question is: When does it end and how does it end?”

Her father, who still serves as the Appeals of Conscience Foundation’s president, fled Budapest and arrived in the United States in 1947.  He founded the organization to promote religious freedom, human rights, peace and inter-religious dialogue across the globe and received the Presidential Citizens Medal from then-President Bill Clinton in 2001.

Schneier Dresbach also referred to the recent “premeditated” alleged hate crime committed at Central Synagogue by wacko Larry Montes. The antisemite barged into the house of worship on Lexington Avenue and East 55th Street during a Shabbat service — and allegedly attacked a congregant and a security guard, unleashing chaos on the peaceful place.

“It’s very premeditated. When somebody says, ‘Oh, the guy who ran into Central Synagogue was a crazy person.’ He wasn’t so crazy,” Schneier Dresbach said.

“If he was crazy, he would have gone out anywhere in the street and yelled. He specifically picked a synagogue.”

Mamdani’s office had no immediate comment on Schneier Dresbach’s accusations.

But the mayor has said he has “zero tolerance” for antisemitism or any kind of bigotry and has dedicated more funds to address it.

“The Mamdani administration will continue using every tool at our disposal to stamp out hatred and build a city where every New Yorker is not only safe, but feels a true sense of inclusion and belonging,” a Mamdani spokesperson told The Post last week.
